question.:question/problem:
Consider the matrix $C,$ given by

$$
C=\begin{bmatrix}2 & -3 & 4 \\ -5 & 1 & 7 \\ 3 & 8 & -2\end{bmatrix}.
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on $C?$

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's list the required operations:

- The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1}$ means that we need to add $1$ times the first row to the second row.

- The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{3}$ means that we need to add $2$ times the third row to the second row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =\begin{bmatrix}2 & -3 & 4 \\ -5 & 1 & 7 \\ 3 & 8 & -2\end{bmatrix}\quad {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & \sim \begin{bmatrix}2 & -3 & 4 \\ -5+(1)(2) & 1+(1)(-3) & 7+(1)(4) \\ 3 & 8 & -2\end{bmatrix} \\  & \sim \begin{bmatrix}2 & -3 & 4 \\ -3 & -2 & 11 \\ 3 & 8 & -2\end{bmatrix}\quad {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{3} \\  & \sim \begin{bmatrix}2 & -3 & 4 \\ -3+(2)(3) & -2+(2)(8) & 11+(2)(-2) \\ 3 & 8 & -2\end{bmatrix} \\  & \sim \begin{bmatrix}2 & -3 & 4 \\ 3 & 14 & 7 \\ 3 & 8 & -2\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{1}\leftrightarrow{R}_{2}$ on $A?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The operation ${R}_{1}\leftrightarrow{R}_{2}$ means that we need to swap the first and second rows.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\begin{bmatrix}2 & -3 & 4 \\ -5 & 1 & 7 \\ 3 & 8 & -2\end{bmatrix}\quad {R}_{1}\leftrightarrow{R}_{2} \\ & \sim \begin{bmatrix}-5 & 1 & 7 \\ 2 & -3 & 4 \\ 3 & 8 & -2\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1}$ on $A?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The operation ${R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1}$ means that we need to multiply the first row of the matrix by $\frac{1}{3}.$

Multiplying the first row by $\frac{1}{3}$, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\begin{bmatrix}6 & -6 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 5 & 6\end{bmatrix}\quad {R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\ & \sim \begin{bmatrix}\frac{1}{3}\cdot (6) & \frac{1}{3}\cdot (-6) & \frac{1}{3}\cdot (0) \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 5 & 6\end{bmatrix} \\ & \sim \begin{bmatrix}2 & -2 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 5 & 6\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$
